cards.target: Pahalı bir restoran yerine ucuz ve lezzetli bir lokanta bulduk.
cards.english: Instead of an expensive restaurant we found a cheap and delicious eatery.

cards.target: Tuvaleti kullanabilir miyim?
cards.english: May I use the bathroom?

cards.target: Bu yer boş mu?
cards.english: Is this place empty?
cards.existing: Person suffix attaches to `mi`, not the verb: `gidecek misin?` (will you go?), not `gideceksin mi`. The question particle steals the person ending.

cards.target: Onlar yakında hastaneye gidecekler.
cards.english: They will go to the hospital soon.
cards.existing: Future can also be prediction or intention, not just a fixed plan. yağmur yağacak (it will rain), umarım gelecek (I hope she comes).

cards.target: O yakında hastaneye gidecek.
cards.english: He/She will go to the hospital soon.

cards.target: Onlar yakında ofiste alacaklar.
cards.english: They will buy at the office soon.

cards.target: Az önce yemeği pişirmeyi bitirdi.
cards.english: She just finished cooking dinner.

cards.target: Biz dün akşam ofiste bulduk.
cards.english: We found at the office last night.

cards.target: Onlar geçen hafta mutfaktan başladılar.
cards.english: They started in the kitchen last week.

cards.target: Sen geçen yıl müzede verdin.
cards.english: You gave in the museum last year.
cards.existing: Spacing matters: write `mi` separately from the verb. Computer keyboards make it tempting to glue them – don't. `geliyor mu` two words, `geliyormusun` is broken.

cards.target: Ben önceki gün evde verdim.
cards.english: I gave at home the day before.

cards.target: Onlar geçen hafta ofiste rapor yazdı.
cards.english: They wrote a report at the office last week.

cards.target: Sen geçen hafta bunu mutfakta söyledin.
cards.english: You said this in the kitchen last week.

cards.target: Sen geçen yıl mutfakta başladın.
cards.english: You started in the kitchen last year.

cards.target: Kutuda on iki yumurta var.
cards.english: There are twelve eggs in the box.
cards.existing: Combined with the possessive: `arabam var` (I have a car – 'my-car there is'). Different structure than the locative form, both valid.

cards.target: Pencereyi açar mısınız?
cards.english: Would you mind opening the window?
cards.existing: Picking the form: harmonise with the last vowel of the question target. After 'a/ı' → mı, 'e/i' → mi, 'o/u' → mu, 'ö/ü' → mü.

cards.target: Yemekler saat altıda hazırlanır.
cards.english: The food is prepared at six o'clock.
cards.existing: Why this matters: getting the suffix vowel wrong is the #1 marker of foreign-sounding Turkish. The root's last vowel blocks certain suffix shapes.

cards.target: Kelebek çiçekten çiçeğe uçtu.
cards.english: The butterfly flew from flower to flower.
cards.existing: Turkish goes Subject-Object-Verb: the verb is the final word. `Ben kitap okuyorum` = 'I book am-reading' = 'I'm reading a book'. The verb wraps everything up.

cards.target: Çiftçi sebzeleri pazarda sattı.
cards.english: The farmer sold the vegetables at the market.

cards.target: Turistler baklavayı restoranda yedi.
cards.english: The tourists ate the baklava at the restaurant.

cards.target: Başkan tiyatroda romanı bitirdi.
cards.english: The president finished the novel at the theater.

cards.target: Sen ileride ofiste yazacaksın.
cards.english: You will write at the office in the future.

cards.target: Sen birazdan markette yazacaksın.
cards.english: You will write at the market in a moment.

cards.target: O birazdan markette bitecek.
cards.english: He/She will finish at the market in a moment.

cards.target: Sen ileride havaalanında okuyacaksın.
cards.english: You will read at the airport in the future.

cards.target: Siz birazdan markette okuyacaksınız.
cards.english: You (formal) will read at the market in a moment.

cards.target: Biz önceki gün müzede söyledik.
cards.english: We said in the museum the day before.
cards.existing: Yes/no questions use a separate particle: `mi / mı / mu / mü` (vowel harmony). It floats after the questioned word: `Geliyor musun?` (Are you coming?).

cards.target: Ben önceki gün ofiste başladım.
cards.english: I started at the office the day before.

cards.target: Sen önceki gün ofiste gördün.
cards.english: You saw at the office the day before.

cards.target: Saat dokuz buçukta toplantımız var.
cards.english: We have a meeting at half past nine.

cards.target: Siz geçen hafta havaalanında başladınız.
cards.english: You (formal) started at the airport last week.

cards.target: Bu film çok ilgi çekecek.
cards.english: This movie will be very interesting.

cards.target: Konya treni saat dokuzda kalkıyor.
cards.english: The train to Konya departs at nine o'clock.

cards.target: Paleontoloji müzesinde kaç fosil sergileniyor?
cards.english: How many fossils are displayed in the paleontology museum?

cards.target: Siz önümüzdeki yıl mutfakta yazacaksınız.
cards.english: You (formal) will write in the kitchen next year.

cards.target: Siz önümüzdeki yıl hastanede yapacaksınız.
cards.english: You (formal) will do at the hospital next year.

cards.target: Yemeği ben pişirdim, umarım beğenirsiniz.
cards.english: I cooked the food, I hope you like it.

cards.target: Küçükken bisiklet sürmeyi çok severdim.
cards.english: When I was little I used to love riding a bicycle.

cards.target: Ben bu aralar plajda ağlıyorum.
cards.english: I've been crying at the beach lately.

cards.target: Kütüphanede nadide el yazması eserler var.
cards.english: There are rare handwritten works in the library.

cards.target: Maç bu akşam saat dokuzda başlayacak.
cards.english: The match will start at nine o'clock tonight.

cards.target: Eczacı soğuk algınlığım için ilaç verdi.
cards.english: The pharmacist gave me medicine for my cold.

cards.target: Arkadaşım Beyoğlu'nda yeni bir restoran açtı.
cards.english: My friend opened a new restaurant in Beyoğlu.
cards.existing: Names get an apostrophe before any suffix: İstanbul'da (in Istanbul), Ankara'ya (to Ankara). The apostrophe keeps the name visible.

cards.target: Küçük çocuk büyük bir dondurma istedi.
cards.english: The small child wanted a big ice cream.

cards.target: Sıcak yaz günlerinde soğuk limonata içeriz.
cards.english: We drink cold lemonade on hot summer days.

cards.target: Yağmur aniden başladı ve hepimiz ıslandık.
cards.english: The rain started suddenly and we all got wet.

cards.target: Kusura bakmayın, yanlış kapıyı çaldım galiba.
cards.english: Sorry, I think I knocked on the wrong door.

cards.target: Bu kışın en soğuk günü bugünmüş.
cards.english: Apparently today is the coldest day of this winter.
cards.existing: `-miş/-mış` = the witnessed-past variant (hearsay, inferred, or surprise). `Gelmiş` = he came (so I hear / apparently). Distinct from `geldi` (I saw him come).

cards.target: Bu ucuz bir gözlük, çok beğendim.
cards.english: These are cheap glasses, I liked them a lot.

cards.target: Otobüse geç kaldığım için koşarak çıktım.
cards.english: I ran out because I was late for the bus.

cards.target: Bilgisayarlarımız çok eski, yenilerini almamız lazım.
cards.english: Our computers are very old, we need to get new ones.

cards.target: Merhaba, bugün hava çok güzel ve sıcak.
cards.english: Hello, the weather is very nice and warm today.

cards.target: Turistler bugün küçük bir restoranda yemek yedi.
cards.english: The tourists ate at a small restaurant today.

cards.target: Ali dün ormanda çadırını tamir etti.
cards.english: Ali repaired his tent in the forest yesterday.

cards.target: Çiçekler kışın kurudu ama baharda tekrar açtı.
cards.english: The flowers dried in winter but opened again in spring.

cards.target: Park ile okul arasında bir fırın var.
cards.english: There is a bakery between the park and the school.

cards.target: Komşumuz dün film izledi ve çok yoruldu.
cards.english: Our neighbor watched a movie yesterday and got very tired.

cards.target: Bu restoranda porsiyon büyük ve fiyatlar uygun.
cards.english: Portions are big and prices are reasonable at this restaurant.

cards.target: Anneannem bu sabah alışveriş merkezinde neşeyle gülüyor.
cards.english: My grandmother is smiling cheerfully at the shopping mall this morning.

cards.target: Botanik bahçesinde yüzlerce farklı bitki türü var.
cards.english: There are hundreds of different plant species in the botanical garden.

cards.target: Vahadaki çeşmede berrak ve serin su akar.
cards.english: Clear and cool water flows from the fountain in the oasis.

cards.target: Saat tam on ikide öğle yemeği molası var.
cards.english: There's a lunch break at exactly twelve o'clock.

cards.target: Eski evimiz küçüktü ama çok sıcak ve samimiydi.
cards.english: Our old house was small but very warm and cozy.

cards.target: Şöminenin yanında yumuşak bir battaniye ve yastık var.
cards.english: There is a soft blanket and pillow next to the fireplace.
cards.existing: `-miş` (with harmony) marks inferred or reported past: `gelmiş` = 'apparently came / I heard he came / it seems he came'. English needs auxiliaries; Turkish bakes it into one suffix.

cards.target: Bu eski bina yıkılacak ve yerine yenisi yapılacak.
cards.english: This old building will be demolished and a new one built in its place.

cards.target: Bu kış çok sert geçiyor, her gün kar yağıyor.
cards.english: This winter is very harsh, it snows every day.

cards.target: İki yüz elli gram tereyağı lazım bu tarif için.
cards.english: Two hundred fifty grams of butter is needed for this recipe.

cards.target: Her sabah bir bardak süt içerim, sağlık için iyi.
cards.english: I drink a glass of milk every morning, it's good for health.

cards.target: Öğrenciler hafta içi plaja gitmek için izin aldı.
cards.english: The students got permission to go to the beach during the week.

cards.target: Konser salonunda akustik mükemmel ve atmosfer büyüleyici.
cards.english: The acoustics are perfect and the atmosphere is enchanting in the concert hall.
cards.existing: Person suffix attaches to `mi`, not the verb: `gidecek misin?` (will you go?), not `gideceksin mi`. The question particle steals the person ending.

cards.target: Deniz kenarında sessiz bir atmosfer var, çok huzurlu.
cards.english: By the seaside there's a quiet atmosphere, very peaceful.

cards.target: Bu yarımada ile şu balta arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this peninsula and that axe.

cards.target: Bu boza ile şu kanepe arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this boza and that sofa.
cards.existing: Combined with the possessive: `arabam var` (I have a car – 'my-car there is'). Different structure than the locative form, both valid.

cards.target: Bu veritabanı ile şu bent arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this database and that dam.

cards.target: Bu ceylan ile şu robot arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this gazelle and that robot.

cards.target: Bu brokoli ile şu drone arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this broccoli and that drone.
cards.existing: Combined with the possessive: `arabam var` (I have a car – 'my-car there is'). Different structure than the locative form, both valid.

cards.target: İki gözüm var.
cards.english: I have two eyes.

cards.target: Kulaklarım var.
cards.english: I have ears.

cards.target: Yeni ayakkabılarım var.
cards.english: I have new shoes.
